payload.label: Read an export of my conversations
payload.job: Read an export of the person's conversations (a chat app's saved messages, a mailbox page or email file, the Messages database, an AI assistant's logs or a captured web chat) from a folder they chose, and give each conversation's messages in order, ready to be kept as the person's messages
payload.description: Runs on the person's computer over the folder they granted it to read, and reads only inside it. Give file (a path inside the folder). source names the kind of export (tool:list-the-kinds-of-conversation-export-i-can-read gives them); left out, the file is matched to a kind by what it looks like and a file two kinds could read is refused with their names. sources_file is a file in the folder holding the person's own kinds ({ sources: [row] }): a kind is a row of field names, so a new export is a new row, not new code. descriptor holds the run's own choices: mailbox_address (which address is the person's, for mail), expected_provider (for a captured web chat), source_ref (what to call this source), app (the name the conversations are kept under). mode all (the default) returns the whole export a page of atoms at a time (limit, cursor); threads returns the list of threads, newest first; page returns one thread's newest messages first from before_cursor, for a very large single log (session_id, limit). Returns threads and atoms (the canonical contract: each atom has a stable atom_ref that does not change when its words are edited), conversations ({ conversation_id, title, app, messages: [{ id, speaker, text, at }] }, speaker person, ai or the name the source showed, only what was said, a time only where the source gave one) in the shape the owner that keeps messages takes a chat read off its page, rejections (one structured entry for each thing the export could not give), next_cursor where there is more. Keeps nothing: hand conversations to the owner that keeps messages.

file.description: The export, a path inside the granted folder

source.description: The kind of export (an id from the list of kinds); left out, matched by what the file looks like

sources_file.description: A file in the folder holding the person's own kinds: { sources: [row] }

mailbox_address.description: The person's own address, for mail: which words are theirs

expected_provider.description: For a captured web chat: the provider the capture must be from

app.description: The name the conversations are kept under

cursor.description: Where the next page starts: the next_cursor of the answer before

session_id.description: mode page: which thread of the file

before_cursor.description: mode page: the next_cursor of the page after this one

erase_action.confirm: Forget this message? Replies and results that quoted it keep their own words.

src/person-store.mjs recordFileArrival: a file that arrived (a camera clip, an upload)
src/thread-summaries.mjs: an AI's summary of one conversation and the message it covers through

indexes._read_by: src/messages.mjs unnamedSpeakers and capturedTurns (the same bounded speaker window carries capture provenance; no separate capture index or prompt read after backfill)

indexes.name: kept

indexes._read_by: src/resource-input-capture.mjs bounded resource alarm and claim recovery

payload.label: Kinds of conversation export I can read
payload.job: List the kinds of conversation export that can be read (chat apps, email, the Messages database, AI assistant logs, captured web chats), what each one's files look like and what the run must say for it
payload.description: Returns said (the count and the ids, in a line) and sources: each { id, label, format, reader, needs, app, files_look_like }. id is what source takes in tool:read-an-export-of-my-conversations; needs lists the choices the run must make for that kind (mailbox_address for mail, expected_provider for a captured web chat); app is the name its conversations are kept under; files_look_like is what a file of that kind holds, which is how a file is matched to its kind when none is named. A kind not listed is a new row in a file of the person's own.

payload.label: List the conversation sources on this computer
payload.job: Find every app's conversations on this computer (AI chat exports, Google Takeout activity, and the sessions local AI apps keep) and say how many files of each there are
payload.description: Runs on the person's computer over the folder they granted it to read (their home folder), and reads only inside it. For each kind of source (read-data/conversation-sources-on-this-computer.json: ChatGPT, Claude.ai and Grok account exports, Google Takeout activity for Gemini Apps, Assistant and AI Mode, and the sessions of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Hermes) it answers how many files are here, their bytes and the first of them. more_places adds folders to look for exports in. Keeps nothing and reaches no records.

payload.label: Import my conversations from one source
payload.job: Bring every conversation of one app (an AI chat export, Google Takeout activity, or a local AI app's sessions) from this computer into my records completely, one row per conversation and every message, continuing where an earlier run stopped
payload.description: Runs on the person's computer over the folder they granted (their home folder). source is one id tool:list-the-conversation-sources-on-this-computer gives; files, when given, names the files (paths in the folder) instead of looking for them. Each conversation is kept as the person's messages (record message, with its source key, so bringing it in again adds nothing twice) and one row of their AI conversations list (record:ai-conversation: title, app, conversation, started, last, messages, models, original_file; labels, people, pursuits and follow-ups they set are never touched). Writes go through the records door in batches; a busy (503) or slow door is asked again after a growing wait with the same request key. Each file has a cursor row (conversation-import-cursor) that moves only past what was kept, so a run that stops, or reaches time_box_seconds, answers more: true and the next run goes on from there; a file already done and unchanged is skipped. Files the messages carried are copied into the person's files through the files door under /messages: an export's file (ChatGPT's file-XXXX, Grok's asset) found beside the export as /messages/<app>/<name>, an image pasted into a session as /messages/<conversation>/<message>-<n>; a file already there with the same bytes is not written again, and a file not found beside the export is counted (attachments_not_kept), never an error.

folder.description: A folder in the granted home folder, like Downloads/old-exports

attachments.description: Where a message's file is when it is not beside the export: { attachment id (file-XXXX): a path in the granted folder }

home.description: The home folder the AI apps' session folders are under, when the grant holds only those folders instead of the whole home; the granted folder must be inside it, and a read still reaches only what was granted

changed_within_days.description: Only the files changed within this many days (old Trillion's recorder swept the sessions changed within 7); without it every file is read

time_box_seconds.description: How long this run may keep going, in seconds (at most 3000); past it the run saves where it is and answers more: true
